review.condition: the run record is evidence of an approved contract and its sprints; each sprint takes the ordinary Ticket gates
the file decides what canonical means, so two implementations agree or disagree by these bytes rather than by the prose; it is reviewed with the contract whose serialization it pins
explanatory only; its facts are validated against canonical records rather than reviewed for correctness
each patch is reviewed with the ticket that produced it, and the manifest pins the series identity; the qualification workflow rebuilds the recorded tree from the pinned upstream
the registry records measured cost; it is append-only and its prefix checkpoint is what is reviewed
a grant is minted by the host, not authored
the manifest records positions and a recommendation; the decision it leads to takes its own lifecycle
an example is read by the validator that ships with its contract; a refused example earns its place by being refused
reviewed with the contract it closes; the bytes that change here are the bytes that decide, so no editorial exemption applies
a diagram describes; it defines nothing on its own
the state is recorded by the host, not authored
the base is computed from an approved manifest, not authored
the registry records a review; it is not itself reviewed by a panel
the record proves a run's isolation; it is not itself panel-reviewed
the report is read by the operator who approves the deletions named in it
reviewed with the ticket that produced it; an escalated iteration is read by whoever owns the trigger
the record is evidence of a step; it is not itself panel-reviewed
each entry excuses a guard from the mutation run, so an addition is reviewed as the claim it is
the pass proposes; an accepted governance change is its own artifact and takes the full panel
the enumeration is extracted from the resume contract, so a change to it is a change to that table and is reviewed with it
configuration is never editorial: the `-text` attribute is what keeps a pinned patch checksum stable across platforms
the record carries the panels and the user decisions it cites; it is not itself panel-reviewed
the record proves what an installed extension wrote and under which capability; it is not itself panel-reviewed
a single independent cross-family code review per issue #18, not a four-model panel; the panel reviews planning and behavior-defining documents, and code takes the review that reads code
the result is evidence bound to a candidate; its findings are disposed in the canonical triage
reviewed with the ticket that produced it; a committed harness additionally takes a cross-family code review
the published half of a daemon keypair; the signing half never enters the repository, and a validator refuses one that does
